section.title: Introduction
section.p: MakeQRCode provides a relocatable module interface for creating QR codes. It is intended for applications and other modules that need to generate QR code images without invoking a command-line tool or duplicating QR code generation code.

The module converts text, binary data, or explicitly described QR segments into an opaque workspace block. That block can then be rendered as a RISC OS sprite or as a packed bitmap. For common callers, a single simple interface encodes text and returns a sprite in one operation.

The internal representation of QR codes is private to the module. Callers must not inspect, modify, copy in part, or persist assumptions about the contents of an opaque workspace block. The block may only be passed back to MakeQRCode SWIs that document that they accept it.

section.title: Overview
section.p: QR codes are two-dimensional barcodes made from a square grid of light and dark modules. A scanner reads the modules to recover a sequence of data. In common use that data is a text string, but it may also be arbitrary bytes or a sequence of structured QR segments.
In QR terminology, a module is one square cell of the QR matrix. This is distinct from a RISC OS relocatable module such as MakeQRCode itself.

QR codes do not store images or application actions directly. They store data which the scanning software interprets. A web address may be opened in a browser, a contact string may be offered as an address book entry, and a wireless network string may be offered as network settings, but those behaviours are conventions implemented by the scanner.
For a broader introduction to QR codes, see the .

subsection.title: QR version
subsection.p: The QR version controls the size of the QR matrix. Version 1 is 21 by 21 modules; each later version adds four modules in each direction, up to version 40 at 177 by 177 modules. Larger versions can hold more data, but produce a denser and larger code. Allowing the module to choose the smallest suitable version usually gives the best result.

subsection.title: ECC level
subsection.p: ECC is error correction coding. A higher ECC level allows the QR code to survive more damage, dirt, or poor scanning conditions, but leaves less room for payload data. The levels are:

value-table.value: Lowest redundancy; holds the most data.
Higher redundancy and the default used by MakeQRCode.
Highest redundancy; holds the least data.

subsection.p: ECC boosting allows the encoder to raise the ECC level when doing so does not force a larger QR version.

subsection.title: Mask pattern
subsection.p: A mask pattern changes how the generated modules are inverted to avoid visual patterns that are hard for scanners to read. QR codes define eight mask patterns. Automatic mask selection asks the encoder to test the patterns and choose a good one. Fixed masks are mainly useful for testing or for callers that need repeatable output.

value-table.value: Use the specified QR mask pattern.

subsection.title: Segments
subsection.p: A QR payload may be split into segments. Each segment has a mode that describes how its data should be encoded. Numeric and alphanumeric modes are compact for their restricted character sets, byte mode is suitable for general data, ECI segments identify the character set or interpretation used by following data, and kanji mode is used for Shift JIS kanji data.

Segment control is more complex than text or binary input, but it can reduce the QR version needed for structured data. It is usually only needed by callers that already understand the QR standard or need precise compatibility with another encoder.

subsection.title: Common payload strings
subsection.p: Many scanners recognise text strings with conventional prefixes. MakeQRCode does not interpret these strings; it encodes them exactly as supplied. Useful examples include:

definition-table.definition: An email address or email message.
A text message destination and optional body.

item.p: To create a sprite with the simple interface, call with a text string, optional sprite controls, and an output buffer.
To create a sprite with the advanced interface, call to create an opaque workspace block, then call with sprite output selected.
To create a bitmap with the advanced interface, call to create an opaque workspace block, then call with packed bitmap output selected.
To control QR segments directly, call to create an opaque workspace block, optionally call it again with the append flag to add more segments, then call to create the required image data.

subsection.title: Buffer handling
subsection.p: SWIs that return variable sized data take an output buffer pointer and an output buffer length in registers. If the output buffer pointer is 0, or if the supplied length is 0, the SWI performs a size query and returns the number of bytes required without writing output.

If the supplied buffer is too small, the SWI returns the error and returns the number of bytes required in the output length register. If the SWI succeeds, the same register contains the number of bytes written.
Buffer contents are undefined when an error is returned, except for errors reported by a size query, where no output bytes are written.

subsection.title: Encoding controls
subsection.p: The encoding controls block is used by SWIs that create an opaque workspace block. If a pointer to this block is 0, the default values are used.

offset-table.offset: Size of this block in bytes (24 for the full block). Fields beyond this size are treated as absent.
Error correction level. See the ECC level table. The default is 2.
Minimum QR version, in the range 1 to 40. The default is 1.
Maximum QR version, in the range 1 to 40. The default is 40.
Mask pattern. See the mask pattern table. The default is -1.
Encoding flags. Bit 0 set permits the module to raise the ECC level when this does not increase the QR version. The default is set. Other bits must be zero.

subsection.title: Sprite controls
subsection.p: The sprite controls block is used by . It combines the encoding controls with sprite rendering controls. If a pointer to this block is 0, the default values are used.

offset-table.offset: Size of this block in bytes (48 for the full block). Fields beyond this size are treated as absent.
RISC OS palette word for dark modules. The default is &hex;00000010.
RISC OS palette word for light modules. The default is &hex;FFFFFF10.
Quiet-zone border in QR modules. The default is 4.
Sprite name. The default is qrcode. The name is padded with zero bytes if shorter than 12 bytes.
As for the encoding controls block.
As for the encoding controls block.
As for the encoding controls block.
As for the encoding controls block.
As for the encoding controls block.

subsection.title: Render controls
subsection.p: The render controls block is used by . If a pointer to this block is 0, the default values are used.

offset-table.offset: Size of this block in bytes (32 for the full block). Fields beyond this size are treated as absent.
RISC OS palette word for dark modules in sprite output. The default is &hex;00000010.
RISC OS palette word for light modules in sprite output. The default is &hex;FFFFFF10.
Quiet-zone border in QR modules. The default is 4.
Sprite name for sprite output. The default is qrcode.
Row alignment for packed bitmap output, in bytes. 0 means the module default. The initial default is word alignment.

subsection.title: Render formats
subsection.p: Render format values are used by .

value-table.value: RISC OS sprite file containing one mode 18 sprite. The output begins with the three-word sprite area header, followed by the single sprite. The sprite area offsets use the usual RISC OS stored offset values, so they are four bytes greater than the byte position in the returned file.
Single RISC OS mode 18 sprite, with a two-entry palette and no mask. The sprite area file header is not included.
Packed 1bpp bitmap, one bit per QR module including the requested border. Bit 0 of each byte is the leftmost pixel of that group of eight pixels.

subsection.title: Segment descriptors
subsection.p: The segment interface is provided for callers that need explicit control over the QR mode used for each part of the payload. The segment descriptor array is read only during the call. Segment data is copied into the opaque workspace block, so no pointers from the descriptors are retained.

offset-table.offset: Size of this descriptor in bytes (24 for the full descriptor).

value-table.value: Upper-case alphanumeric data and the limited QR punctuation set.

offset-table.offset: Pointer to the segment data. This is ignored for ECI segments.
Length of the source data in bytes, except for ECI segments where this is the ECI assignment value.
Number of characters represented by the segment, or 0 to allow the module to derive this for modes where the byte length is sufficient.
Segment flags. Reserved bits must be zero.

subsection.title: Opaque workspace blocks
subsection.p: Opaque workspace blocks contain their own size in their first word. The remainder of the block is private to MakeQRCode. A block is valid only if it was returned by MakeQRCode and is passed back whole. The contents and layout may change between module versions.

swi-definition.name: MakeQRCode_Sprite
swi-definition.description: Encodes text and returns a RISC OS sprite

entry.register-use: Flags. Reserved bits must be zero.
Pointer to a zero-terminated UTF-8 text string.
Pointer to a sprite controls block, or 0 for defaults.
Pointer to the output buffer, or 0 to query the required size.
Length of the output buffer in bytes, or 0 to query the required size.

exit.register-use: Output width in pixels, including the requested border.
Output height in pixels, including the requested border.
Number of bytes written, or number of bytes required if this is a size query or if is returned.

use.p: This SWI is the simple interface for callers that want a QR code sprite from a text string. It encodes the text and renders a sprite in one call. By default it uses ECC quartile, versions 1 to 40, automatic mask choice, ECC boosting, a border of 4 modules, black foreground, white background, and the sprite name qrcode. The output is a RISC OS sprite file containing one sprite.

use.p: This SWI encodes UTF-8 text or binary byte data into an opaque workspace block. The result is not directly renderable by the caller; pass the block to to produce image data. The workspace block contains its own size.

use.p: This SWI renders an opaque workspace block produced by or . Sprite file and single sprite output use RISC OS mode 18 and include a two-entry palette. Packed bitmap output is intended for callers that want to place the image into their own bitmap or sprite format.

swi-definition.name: MakeQRCode_EncodeSegments
swi-definition.description: Encodes explicit QR segments into an opaque workspace block

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Append these segments to the opaque workspace block in R4. Reserved. Must be zero.
Pointer to an array of segment descriptors.
Number of segment descriptors in the array.
Pointer to an encoding controls block, or 0 for defaults. This is ignored when R0 bit 0 is set.
Pointer to the output buffer for the opaque workspace block, or 0 to query the required size. When R0 bit 0 is set, this must point to an existing opaque workspace block.
Length of the output buffer in bytes, or 0 to query the required size. When R0 bit 0 is set, this is the total available length of the buffer containing the existing workspace block.

exit.register-use: Number of bytes written, or number of bytes required if this is a size query or if is returned.

use.p: This SWI is the low-level encoding interface for callers that need to control the QR mode of each payload segment. It returns the same opaque workspace block format as .

If R0 bit 0 is clear, this SWI starts a new opaque workspace block and uses the encoding controls in R3. If R0 bit 0 is set, R4 must point to an existing opaque workspace block previously returned by MakeQRCode. The supplied segment descriptors are appended to that block, and the original encoding controls in the block continue to apply.

Appending may be used to build a QR payload incrementally. For an append size query, R4 still points to the existing opaque workspace block and R5 is 0. If there is not enough space to append the supplied segments, the error is returned, R5 contains the required total size, and the existing workspace block remains valid and unchanged.

command-definition.name: MakeQRCode
command-definition.description: Creates a QR code sprite file
command-definition.parameter: The text to encode into the QR code. Use quotes if the text contains spaces.

use.p: The command creates a RISC OS sprite file containing one QR code sprite. It uses the simple interface defaults: ECC quartile, automatic mask choice, ECC boosting, a border of 4 modules, black foreground, white background, and the sprite name qrcode.
The supplied output buffer was too small. The output length register contains the number of bytes required.
Reserved flag bits were set in R0 or in a parameter block.
A supplied pointer, length, version, mask, ECC level, colour, sprite name, or other parameter was invalid.
The input data cannot be encoded within the requested QR version range and ECC level.
The opaque workspace block supplied to was not recognised or was not complete.
The module could not allocate temporary workspace required to complete the operation.

p.extended-example:
REM Query the size required for a default sprite
SYS "XMakeQRCode_Sprite", 0, text%, 0, 0, 0 TO ,,,,needed%; flags%
IF flags% AND 1 THEN ERROR 0, "Size query failed"
DIM sprite% needed%-1
SYS "MakeQRCode_Sprite", 0, text%, 0, sprite%, needed% TO ,,,,used%
